leftEvidence.title: Lifted up as Moses lifted the serpent

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Jesus compares the Son of Man being lifted up with Moses lifting the serpent and continues with statements about love, sending, and salvation.
points.right: Troubled speech about the hour leads to prayer, a heavenly voice, crowd questions, and a final summons to walk in the light.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The passage materially bears on the Crucifixion while leaving part of its motive, mechanism, or later significance unstated.
points.right: The crowd recognizes death language in the saying but cannot reconcile it with what it has heard about the Christ.

payload.posture: John uses lifted-up language in two distinct settings and later explains that it signals the kind of death Jesus would die.

rightEvidence.title: The kind of death signaled by being lifted up

payload.tension: The earlier passage compares the Son of Man with Moses’ serpent; the later passage adds hour, voice, judgment, attraction, and narrated explanation.
payload.title: Serpent lifted / death signaled
